title: How approximate 2024 crash-zone positions affect ward assignment and ward rankings
method: Each zone is moved to a point drawn uniformly from the disc of its stated accuracy around its placed point, re-assigned to a legacy ward by point-in-polygon, and the fatal crashes counted in zones, ward totals and ranks are recomputed. 2000 simulations, seed 20261022. Ranks are competition ranks among wards with a total above zero (ties share the better rank). Counts per zone are fixed at the printed values; a zone that prints no count contributes nothing.
caveats: This tests sensitivity to the stated accuracy (150 m to 5 km). That accuracy is the project's estimate, not a measured error: the true error may be larger and need not be uniform within the disc.
The ward boundaries are the legacy 290 (DataMeet), not the current 250, and have their own error; a zone near a boundary is sensitive to both.
Only position is varied. The printed counts, the zone list itself (which changes every year) and the zones the report does not name are not.
A ward rank is a range, not a point: read the 5th to 95th percentile columns, not the baseline rank alone.
